newsitem.title: RWANDA: U.N. envoy to discuss foreign force with Rwanda.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy to discuss foreign force with Rwanda.

text.p: The U.N. special envoy for the Zaire crisis returned on Saturday to Rwanda where leaders say a U.N.-backed multinational force is unnecessary because Hutu refugees are flooding home.
"I want to talk to the president and vice-president of Rwanda today," Raymond Chretien told reporters on arrival.
Asked if a change of mandate for the Canadian-led force was needed, Chretien replied: "They will tell me what their position is and I will certainly report it back to the U.N."
The U.N. Security Council gave its formal endorsement to the mutinational force late on Friday and the first contingents could be on the ground within days.

Rwanda said the force was obsolete before it had even been deployed because of the dramatic change that began on Friday -- the mass return of hundreds of thousands of Rwandan Hutus who have lived in Zaire as refugees since 1994.
So far about one-third of the 1.1 million refugees in eastern Zaire are crossing or waiting to cross the border back to Rwanda.
Hundreds of thousands more are far to the south and nothing is known about their condition or intentions.
Chretien, on a non-stop shuttle between regional capitals, said in Kigali the force was still needed.
"Everywhere I go they tell me only such a humanitarian military presence can deal with the problemn of refugees.
"Everywhere I have been told that if the force leaves in four months and the refugees are still there it will have failed in its mission," he said.
"Everybody in the region wants to tackle this big issue of the refugees otherwise forget about peace in the region."
